posts.body_html: Some new pics of S. flava 'super extreme red throat' Bay Co, FL. To recap, this particular clone, unlike the regular extreme red throats, not only has an amazing red throat, but also the body can turn solid red under ideal conditions. This thing looks incredible, but it's giving me a hard time, can't get the body to color up for whatever reason. Nevertheless, still jaw dropping! Pics taken 5/6/20:

posts.body_html:
S. flava "super extreme red throat" is a stupendous plant. You've gotta see it to believe it, really. Very interesting shape to the pitchers too. This is only my second season with it so it's got a fair bit of growing up to do, but it's a stunner already.


Looks innocent enough from above...



...but there's a bloodbath underneath. Look at the amount of color on even the very smallest traps--that's one of the most impressive things about it I think. The following pic is completely unedited, by the way. That color is straight outta the camera.



Thanks for this beaut, meizzwang! Can't wait to see it get bigger (and make some gnarly crosses with it...)

Some more pics of some ERT's, (homies) Pull-ease! Lots of diversity in this population.

Never really paid much attention to this trait, but look at the first three pics below: the body on the outside of the trap is completely green, without veins or red pigmentation! Never noticed this:


Well, mostly green, I think there's a slight red vein up in this pic, but still, it looks pretty cool, guys:




and then the everyday ERT. Even when you've grown these for a very long time, they're still impressive:
